title: Pick your own starting point
hook: What if the form requires a decision instead of supplying one?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish active choice from opt-in and opt-out enrollment.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish active choice from opt-in and opt-out enrollment.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy enrollment system records 60 explicit choices and 40 automatic enrollments. How many enrollments were explicit choices? Toy inputs A=[60, 40]; B=[60, 0].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[100, 60, 40], [60, 60, 0]]. Labels: Total enrolled, Explicit, Automatic.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The same enrollment count can contain different mixtures of active decisions and automatic outcomes. The comparison removes automatic enrollment while preserving explicit choices. Participation alone cannot tell you how each person chose.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Answered=60, Automatic=0. What is Explicit? Answer: 60.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Answered=60, Automatic=0. What is Explicit?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 60. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Requiring new hires to actively choose raised participation about 28 percentage points versus opt-in (Carroll, Choi, Laibson, Madrian & Metrick, 2009).
sourceProvenance.pointer: 500-behavioral-economics-findings.md entry 67: Carroll, Choi, Laibson, Madrian & Metrick, 2009
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish active choice from opt-in and opt-out enrollment.
